transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-12
Time: 11:00 AM PT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Vasquez (Redwood Solutions), Lena Ortiz (Aerodyne CTO), Marcus Hale (Aerodyne Lead ML Eng), Priya Singh (Aerodyne Platform Eng), Diego Ramos (Aerodyne SRE)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Scoping POC for capacity + autoscale: customer needs reserved GPU baseline with burst to shared capacity, fallback policies to smaller model.
- Success criteria: p95 latency < 250ms for chat workloads, 200 concurrent requests sustained for peak, identical output quality vs baseline model, cost estimates acceptable.
- Actions: Redwood to send pricing and benchmark scripts; customer to share prompts and traffic shapes; schedule benchmark run.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: All right everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Maya, AE, and Ravi is our SE. we'll walk through how we'd size the POC, reserved GPUs, burst and fallback strategies, and then capture success criteria.
[00:14] Lena Ortiz: Hi, thanks. we'll be quick 
d we want to validate the whole inference profile before committing to Dedicated. our main use case is customer support summarization and reranking pipelines.
[00:25] Marcus Hale: yes and important to note we have mixed workloads: short chat messages (avg 60 tokens) and longer summarization jobs (avg 800 tokens) that run in batch overnight.
[00:38] Ravi Patel: got it. so three main questions for scoping: 1) baseline reserved capacity sizing, 2) autoscale/burst strategy for spikes, and 3) fallback policies and rollouts. do these map to what you expect?
[00:47] Priya Singh: exactly. and we have compliance constraints for the pilot 
d if possible we'd like VPC peering and use customer KMS.
[00:56] Maya Chen: yep we can do Private POC with customer-managed KMS. samir will follow up on packaging.
[01:05] Diego Ramos: a quick transcribe note 
d last time someone said V-P-C as VPC, sorry.
[01:10] Ravi Patel: (laughs) we all do it. okay diving into sizing. Based on the traffic numbers Marcus shared earlier (we got the CSV), you have peak concurrent 200 requests, p95 latency goal 250ms for chat, and batch throughput requirement ~10K tokens/sec overnight. is that still accurate?
[01:28] Marcus Hale: yeah those are the targets; p50 is fine <100ms. we can tolerate some increased latency during deep batches but not above 2s.
[01:38] Ravi Patel: great. For reserved pool, we typically recommend sizing for steady-state concurrent load 
d e.g., reserve capacity for 150 concurrent chat requests with headroom for model KV cache warmups. For your model (we discussed a 7B trimmed open model), a single H100-equivalent instance with X inference slots handles approx 40 concurrent short-chat sessions at ~120 tokens/sec each 
d so to cover 150 conc you'd reserve about 4 instances (rough estimate).
[02:05] Marcus Hale: when you say 4 instances, is that H100 or A100? our infra cost sensitivity 
d H100 is expensive.
[02:12] Ravi Patel: right, we can recommend either. H100 gives better throughput for large sequence lengths and mixed workloads. A100s are common for cost balance. if using A100-80GB, we estimate roughly 30-35 concurrent chat slots per GPU for your avg 60-token chats, so you'd need ~5 GPUs reserved. We'll put precise numbers in the sizing doc.
[02:31] Lena Ortiz: okay the reserved baseline is fine; what about burst? we don't want cold-start failures during product launches.
[02:38] Maya Chen: burst works two ways: 1) burst into Redwood shared capacity (hosted pool) if you're on Dedicated+Burst or Hosted POC, or 2) allow autoscale to add more reserved nodes if you're on Dedicated with flexible autoscaling. For Private POC, we can configure a temporary burst policy to a soft limit and notify you.
[02:56] Priya Singh: for security reasons we'd prefer VPC-only and KMS. will Redwood's shared capacity see customer models or data?
[03:04] Ravi Patel: good callout. if data residency or handling is the constraint, we recommend Private POC or Dedicated with burst disabled. If you must allow burst, we can use encrypted in-transit and at-rest, but model artifacts will still be involved. we can also configure token-only pointers and never persist prompts in shared pool. we'll put that in the security note.
[03:21] Marcus Hale: what's the typical scale-up time for burst to add instances? that's critical for spikes.
[03:26] Ravi Patel: autoscale up can happen within ~90-180s depending on pre-warm strategy. If you enable pre-warm slots, scale-up is closer to 30-60s. for really tight p95 SLOs you can reserve a small burst buffer (e.g., 1-2 GPUs) pre-warmed and use shared capacity on top.
[03:42] Maya Chen: also fallback policies 
d we recommend a two-tier fallback: first downgrade to a quantized model variant (same architecture but 8-bit/4-bit) with lower latency but slightly different output characteristics; second fallback to a smaller model family if quantized quality is unacceptable. you should define acceptable quality deltas as part of success criteria.
[03:59] Lena Ortiz: acceptable quality delta 
d how do we measure that? we have a labeled eval set for support answers.
[04:05] Ravi Patel: perfect. we'll run side-by-side A/B benchmarks using your prompt set and compute automatic metrics (exact-match, rouge/bleu where applicable) plus human spot checks. success criteria could be: no more than 3% drop in our primary metric and user-facing impact below threshold.
[04:18] Marcus Hale: can we stress test with a mix: 70% short chat low-latency, 30% long summarization. the long jobs often have big token lengths 
d 800 tokens 
d they tank throughput.
[04:28] Ravi Patel: yes, good to model both. batch windows are ideal for long jobs 
d we can schedule batching in off-peak and use dedicated batch nodes with larger sequence-length optimized kernels. the runtime supports different kernel profiles, so batching long sequences is much more efficient.
[04:41] Samir Vasquez: quick note about KV cache 
d some of the transcription here may say KV cash, but we do use KV cache to keep conversational context hot. warm caches matter: if you can pin active conversations to warm workers that improves latency.
[04:53] Diego Ramos: what's the plan for canaries and rollouts inside POC? we want to ensure we don't regress quality.
[04:59] Ravi Patel: we'll do an incremental rollout. for POC benchmarks run we'll start with 10% traffic on the new config, then 50%, and if metrics pass promote to 100%. Redwood's rollout features let you set automatic rollback on latency or quality regressions.
[05:12] Priya Singh: cool. about observability 
d we need token-level cost and latency breakdown, per-route dashboards, traces. is that included in the POC?
[05:20] Maya Chen: yes we'll enable the Console for the POC 
d cost per token, p95/p99 latency, per-model breakdowns. we'll give you RBAC access and SSO via SAML.
[05:28] Lena Ortiz: timeline question: how long to stand up POC once terms are signed?
[05:33] Maya Chen: for Hosted POC typically 48 hours, Dedicated POC with reserved nodes is ~5 business days for provisioning, Private POC (VPC peering + KMS) is 7-10 business days. we'll put exact timelines in the proposal.
[05:45] Marcus Hale: we want a 4-week POC window; week 1 smoke and baseline, week 2 benchmarks, week 3 run production-ish traffic and validate durability, week 4 finalize SLA and contract.
[05:57] Ravi Patel: that's a common cadence. for benchmarks we'll propose a 24-48 hour continuous load plus a 2-hour peak stress run that simulates release traffic.
[06:07] Marcus Hale: what's your recommended metric set for go/no-go?
[06:10] Ravi Patel: recommended: p95 latency per route, throughput (reqs/sec and tokens/sec), error rate (4xx/5xx), model quality delta vs baseline on your eval set, and cost per 1k tokens. Also operational signals: autoscale event counts, cache hit rates, pre-warm success.
[06:27] Priya Singh: one more: audit logs and retention 
d we need 1 year of audit logs for the pilot.
[06:33] Maya Chen: we can enable extended retention as an add-on; we'll include options.
[06:37] Lena Ortiz: fine. back to sizing detail 
d can you give an example numeric runbook we can use to provision on our end?
[06:44] Ravi Patel: sure. example: if you choose A100-80GB GPUs: reserve 5 A100 GPUs (steady-state) with node sizing: 8 inference slots per GPU for long sequences, 30 slots for short chats 
d these are logical slots. Autoscale policy: scale up when average GPU util >65% for 60s, scale down when util <35% for 5 minutes, max burst to 8 GPUs (reserved + burst). Pre-warm policy: keep 1 GPU pre-warmed during business hours. Fallback: quantized variant endpoint with model-id: aero-7b-q8, then backup model: aero-3b if quantized fails.
[07:24] Marcus Hale: that helps. how do you measure util 
d is it GPU memory or compute util?
[07:28] Ravi Patel: it's a combination; our orchestration uses observable signals: GPU SM utilization and per-request queue length. we tune thresholds per model.
[07:36] Diego Ramos: any gotchas for mixed batch + interactive? we've seen batch starving interactive.
[07:41] Ravi Patel: we recommend separate worker pools for interactive (low-latency) and batch (throughput-optimized). routing policies can send live chat to low-latency pool and long jobs to batch pool. Also priority queuing prevents batch jobs from preempting interactive.
[07:55] Lena Ortiz: cost discussion: how do you charge for reserved vs burst usage in POC?
[08:01] Maya Chen: POC pricing options: 1) fixed reserved fee for baseline + metered burst overage, 2) time-limited full host usage for the pilot. We'll include both in the proposal. For accurate estimates we need the token/sec numbers from Marcus.
[08:12] Marcus Hale: I'll share the token and request histograms.
[08:15] Priya Singh: security paperwork 
d SOC2 and iso we need to review.
[08:19] Maya Chen: we'll attach the security pack in the follow-up including SOC 2 Type II report, penetration test summary, SAML doc, and details on KMS integration.
[08:28] Marcus Hale: ok, final practical question: latency target 250ms p95 for chat 
d do you think that's achievable with the reserve sizes you mentioned?
[08:36] Ravi Patel: yes with reserved + 1 pre-warmed GPU and pinning active convs you'll hit p95 ~180-240ms for 7B family on A100. H100 would be lower. We'll validate in benchmark runs.
[08:49] Samir Vasquez: I'm going to jot down the runbook and we'll publish it to the shared folder.
[08:53] (short crosstalk)
[09:00] Lena Ortiz: ok let's talk about success criteria phrasing in contract: we want 3 things 
d performance, quality, and cost threshold.
[09:08] Maya Chen: propose wording: Performance: p95 latency <250ms for interactive route in steady-state and error rate <0.5%. Quality: quality delta vs baseline on your eval set <=3%. Cost: estimated cost per 1M tokens not to exceed $X (we'll fill after sizing). Those become POC acceptance criteria.
[09:25] Marcus Hale: good. also include acceptance for audit and security docs.
[09:29] Maya Chen: yes.
[09:31] Ravi Patel: next steps recap 
d we'll send the proposal with three pricing options (Hosted POC, Dedicated reserved, Private POC with VPC peering). We'll attach benchmark scripts and a sample load matrix. You (Marcus) will share representative prompts and traffic histograms. We'll target the benchmark next week once scripts are in place.
[09:51] Lena Ortiz: sounds good.
[09:54] Diego Ramos: timeline again 
d I need 7-10 days for Private peering, that might push the POC start but ok.
[09:59] Maya Chen: noted. we'll mark timelines in the doc.
[10:03] (paper rustle)
[10:06] Marcus Hale: any immediate blockers? not from our side except getting the detailed script.
[10:11] Maya Chen: we'll send scripts tomorrow. Ravi, anything else?
[10:15] Ravi Patel: just one more note: when you run benchmarks please include cold-start scenarios for sessions that have been idle 20m, and record KV cache hit rate. that matters a lot for p95.
[10:25] Priya Singh: noted.
[10:27] Maya Chen: great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the proposal and security pack.
[10:32] Lena Ortiz: thanks all.

Meeting end.
